questions.primary_text: Participation to a Study of the impact of AI and explainable AI on Human Performance
questions.secondary_text:
Project Objectives

The aim of this project is to study the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and explainable AI on human performance in carrying out a decision-making task.

What Is Expected of You

You will need to take decisions related to the content of images of geometrical symbols. For each image presented to you, will have to answer a question within a limited time.

You are expected to perform as well as possible. Your performance will be evaluated based on the number of correct answers to evaluated tasks, and your bonus remuneration will be calculated based on this performance. You will be informed when a task is evaluated or not.

Depending on your random assignment into a group, you might receive the assistance of an AI to perform the tasks.

Your Right to Withdraw from the Study

You have the right to withdraw from the study at any time.

Reporting issues

You can report issues at the email adress given at the end of the study, if you detect any.

Confidentiality and Privacy

The information collected in this form is recorded in a file by Jules Leguy for research purposes, specifically to study human performance in a decision making task. The legal basis for this data processing is your consent.

The collected data will only be shared with the following recipients:

  • Jules Leguy
  • Andon Tchechmedjiev

The data will be kept for five years after the scientific publication (expected in 2026). You may request access to your personal data, request corrections, or exercise your right to restrict the processing of your data.

To exercise your rights or ask questions regarding data processing within this framework, you may contact: andon.tchechmedjiev@mines-ales.fr.

Expected Benefits of the Study

Your remuneration will include a fixed part and a variable part.

The fixed part is a payment at an hourly rate of £6. The expected duration of the experiment is 20 minutes, so it should correspond to a £2.0 payment. The actual time used for this calculation will be the median completion time across all participants.

The variable part depends solely on your performance during the experiment. You will receive £0.04 for each correct answer to an evaluated question (not all question will be evaluated, and you will know which ones are evaluated or not). There will be 53 evaluated questions, giving a minimum of £0 and a maximum of £2.12.

In case the measured time is effectively 20 minutes, your remuneration would range from £2.0 to £4.12 depending on your performance. This would correspond to an effective hourly rate ranging between £6 and £12.36.

Possible Risks

The risks involved in these tests are no different from those encountered when performing a standard computer task.

Right to Withdraw Consent

I understand that my participation in this research is voluntary and that I may refuse to participate. If I choose so, I am free to stop participating at any time, without having to provide justification. I will inform the Scientific Supervisor in writing at the following address: jules.leguy@mines-ales.fr.

Color Vision Requirement

This study requires accurate color perception, as the tasks involve distinguishing symbols based on color. For this reason, the protocol screens out participants with colorblindness. You have indicated to Prolific that you are not colorblind. Please only accept this form if that is effectively the case.

Consent
answers: I have read and understand the information contained in this document, and I freely and knowingly consent to participate to this research project. I also confirm that I am not colorblind, as I have indicated on my Prolific profile.
I do not consent to participate to this research project or I am colorblind.

title: Pattern identification tasks
body_text:
The tasks of this protocol will consist in searching whether a pattern (or its rotations) can be found in an image or not.

Below is an example. The pattern to search for contains several symbols, and an empty cell with a question mark. When searching for the pattern, the cell with the question mark can be matched with any symbol (as in the image B), or it can also be matched with an empty cell (as in the image A). In addition, the task consists in searching for rotations of the pattern. The rotations considered are a rotation to the right (symbolized by ↻, as in the image C) or a rotation to the left (symbolized by ↺, as in the image D). In the image E, the pattern or its rotations do not appear.

Please read the information above carefully, as you will not be able to return to this page once you click the button below.

title: Protocol outline
body_text:
The protocol will last about 20 minutes and is organized as follows.


Introduction
First, you will must perform a task that will be used to verify that you understand the instructions. This task will contribute to your bonus remuneration (you will earn £0.04 for each correct answer). It will be the only task of the introduction that does contribute to the bonus remuneration.

To finalize the training, you will then start the preparation phase, which consists in solving a task which will closely resemble those of the main experimental phase.

Main experiment
Then, the main experiment will start. It will be divided into 4 tasks, that will count towards your score and bonus remuneration. Right after each task, you will have to take a survey to give feedback about the task you just performed.

Closing
Finally, you will enter the closing phase, in which you will have to answer a final survey to conclude the protocol.

Please read the information above carefully, as you will not be able to return to this page once you click the button below.

title: Introduction - Main experiment preparation
body_text:
You are now entering the preparation phase for the Main experiment. You are about to perform a task with 5 questions. It will closely resemble the tasks of the Main experiment and is intended to help you practice and prepare for the next phase.

As in the main experimental phase, you will have a limited amount of time to respond to each question. Responding faster will not improve your score. However, if you fail to respond within the alloted time, it will be counted as an error. The allotted time for each question during this training phase is 45 seconds, and it will be shorter for the evaluated tasks in the main experiment.

As this is still a training phase, your score does not count towards your bonus remuneration.

Note that these training tasks are a good opportunity to interact with the AI’s outputs, as there will be less time for such analysis during the main experiment.

Remember to use the in-navigator zoom (ctrl and mouse scroll or ctrl and +/- keys) to adjust the page size if not all elements can be seen at once.

title: Main experiment
body_text:
The introduction is over. You are now entering the main experimental phase. Your performance during this phase will count towards your bonus remuneration. As a reminder, the structure of the experiment is described in the diagram below.


This phase consists in solving 4 tasks. After each task, you must answer a survey directly related to the task you just performed. There are no right or wrong answers to the survey questions; only your score during the tasks will count towards your bonus remuneration.

Please remind that you still have to answer the questions within an alloted time for each image. Responding faster does not improve your score. However, if you fail to respond within the alloted time, it will be counted as an error.

Remember to use the in-navigator zoom (ctrl and mouse scroll or ctrl and +/- keys) to adjust the page size if not all elements can be seen at once.

questions.secondary_text: Which sentence would best describe the strategy you used to maximize your score and monetary bonus?
answers: I largely relied on the AI’s predictions, because I think they were correct all the time or almost all the time.
I largely relied on the AI’s predictions, because I perceived them as imperfect but sufficiently accurate, and not worth the effort to surpass.
I sometimes or often relied on the AI’s predictions, but due to limited trust in the AI, I made efforts to answer independently or to verify its predictions for many questions.
I barely relied or did not rely at all on the AI’s predictions, because I had a very limited trust in the predictions.
I barely relied or did not rely at all on the AI’s predictions, because I wanted to do the task by myself, independently of my assessment of the reliability of the AI.
I did not have a consistent strategy, or my strategy was not described in the propositions above.
